text: One person killed in shooting, police confirm
Police in Washington DC have confirmed one person has been killed in this morning’s shooting and four injured.

“At this time, we have located a total of four individuals that were shot here on the scene, and one individual who is deceased,” Jeffery W Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, told a news conference.
Of the four surviving, one is in critical condition and the other three do not have life-threatening injuries, he said.

Key events6m agoWhite House has been briefed, DC mayor says11m agoSuspect has gunshot wound and is 'contained', police say13m agoOne person killed in shooting, police confirm1h agoMultiple people shot after incident in Washington DC, say police1h agoPolice issue shelter-in-place order after at least five people shot in Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington DC
Vida Fitness has posted a story on Instagram informing members that its Logan Circle location is closed “until further notice” following the shooting.

“The safety and well-being of our members, guests, and team are our highest priorities. We ask that you avoid traveling to the Logan Circle location and surrounding area until further notice. If you are currently in the vicinity, please follow all instructions from local law enforcement,” the post said.
White House has been briefed, DC mayor says
DC mayor Muriel Bowser told the news conference that this was “a senseless act of gun violence”, and that “this lone gunman has been contained”. She also confirmed the White House had been briefed.
At one point in time the suspect had a handgun, but police can’t confirm any other weapons, Carroll said. The suspect was also a member of the gym.
Officers said they believe the suspect barricaded himself into his own apartment and that he shot at officers more than once.
The exact timeline and locations are still to be determined, but the first shooting was reported inside the gym; the exact motivation is still is also yet to be determined.
Police said they believe they know who the suspect is and that he had a conflict with the apartment building.

Carroll said that negotiators made contact with the suspect and had been talking to him for an hour; officers later heard a gunshot, forced entry, and located the suspect suffering from a gunshot wound.
Emergency services have since been rendered, and his status has not been confirmed, Carroll added.
Police are looking into everything and Carroll emphasized that they are “very early in the investigation”.
He added that they believe there was a fire at some point in the building and that it has been put out and contained.
Suspect has gunshot wound and is 'contained', police say
Police discovered the suspect, a white male, with a gunshot wound in a nearby apartment building from where the initial shooting occurred, Carroll said. The suspect is “contained”, he added.
Further to that, NBC News reports that the suspect is barricaded in an apartment building above the gym on 15th Street, citing a federal law enforcement official.
The incident is shifting from an active shooter response to a barricaded subject response, a federal law enforcement official has told NBC News.

It is believed there is no other individual there at scene so this is not considered a hostage situation, they said, adding that it has been about 90 minutes since the suspect fired at law enforcement, which did not strike anyone.
District of Columbia Public Schools has put multiple schools in the vicinity of the shooting on alert status, meaning no one can go in or out of the campuses, but activities inside remain normal.
A post on social media reported that a nearby building appeared to be on fire. The Guardian has not been able to independently verify this claim.
James Spellman was at the gym a little after 8am when he heard shots being fired. He said there were about 50 people in the gym at the time, reported AP.
“Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out,” he said. “One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck.”

Spellman told AP that he and other gym members ran out of the gym, and he said he heard more gunfire in the area of 15th Street. He said he heard about two shots fired in the gym and about five or six fired outside.
Witness Ryan Dubicki was in his nearby apartment around 8 am when, he said, he “heard about five bangs.”
“They were really spread out so I thought it was construction,” he said. It was only a short time later that he looked out “and there were cops everywhere.”
His apartment building managers sent a notice that there was a possible active shooter, reported AP.
Gun violence charity March for Our Lives wrote about the incident online, saying:

double quotation markJust after 8AM, a gunman opened fire at the VIDA Fitness in Logan Circle, right here in Washington, DC. At least five people were shot, the surrounding blocks were locked down, and nearby schools were put on alert. People who walked in for a morning workout found themselves running for their lives and sheltering from gunfire. What should have been an ordinary Thursday morning became a scene none of our neighbors should ever have to carry. This is why we do this work. Gun violence doesn’t just happen somewhere else. Today it happened down the street, and we will not accept it as normal.
The shootings were reported in Logan Circle, about 1 mile north of the White House.

Police urged people to avoid the area of the 1500 block of 15th Street, which includes a VIDA fitness center, St. Luke’s Episcopal Church and residences and is around the corner from a Whole Foods supermarket, the AP reports.
Much of the block was cordoned off. Schools near the scene were placed on lockdown.
Multiple people shot after incident in Washington DC, say police
Multiple people have been shot in north-west Washington DC on Thursday morning, local police have confirmed, prompting a “barricade situation” in the area.
In a statement at 9.21am ET, the DC police said that the incident has “resulted in a barricade situation in the 1500 block of 15th Street, Northwest”.
“Please avoid the area as we work to resolve the incident,” they added.

A Vida Fitness manager told ABC7News that shots were fired outside the business. The local news station reported that as of 9am local time on Thursday morning, the business was still under lockdown and there is police inside the building.
The manager said that they feel safe with police inside, and that the gym will be closed the rest of the day.
Several schools in the area are on lockdown on Thursday morning.
Armed police and members of the National Guard were visible around the Logan Circle area of Washington DC after the incident began on Thursday morning.
Police issue shelter-in-place order after at least five people shot in Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington DC
At least five people have been shot in Northwest Washington DC on Thursday morning, local police confirmed to the Associated Press.
A spokesperson for the Washington DC police department told the Guardian in a brief phone call on Thursday morning that the scene was “still active”. No further details were immediately available.

The DC police department said in a social media post at about 8.20am ET that officers were on the scene responding to an “active shooting in the area of 15th and P Street, Northwest”. The department’s emergency response team was also at the scene. The department urged the public to avoid the area.

The Metropolitan police department has also issued a shelter-in-place order for those in the immediate vicinity of the 1500 block of 15th Street NW. They have urged residents to “go inside to the nearest building, stay away from windows and remain indoors until further notice”.
Local council member Brooke Pinto also posted on social media on Thursday morning that there had been a shooting “at and outside Vida fitness this morning in Logan Circle”.
“Do not go to this area,” Pinto said. “Police looking for suspect.”
A reporter for the Washington Sun said that they spoke with a witness who was in the gym and “heard one gunshot and saw one person down in the gym itself, followed by more shots”.
The person told the reporter that the gym “cleared out” and that people were running from the scene with their “arms raised” as police yelled to clear out.
